clue.text: Unjustified when beginning to exult in praise

indicators.note: the short pieces are placed inside the longer word that follows

parts.note: to bless is to praise, as in blessing God
as in 'as I arrived', meaning when

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: opening letter of exult

explanation.surface: Someone is criticised for starting to crow while being congratulated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When' looks like a time word in the story, but it stands for AS, as in 'as I arrived'.
explanation.definitionFit: A claim without any basis or foundation is groundless, hence not justified.

clue.text: Mass in depth grasped by child

indicators.note: something grasped is held inside the hands of whatever grips it

parts.note: a boy is a male child
d is the standard abbreviation for depth

explanation.surface: A child clutches something heavy that sits deep down.
explanation.definitionFit: A body can mean a large quantity or mass, as in a body of water or evidence.

clue.text: Seekers in vault taken in by prophets

indicators.note: being taken in means being received inside, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: seers foretell the future
a vault is an arched roof, so arch serves as a synonym

explanation.surface: Truth-seekers are welcomed by prophets inside a vaulted chamber.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural nouns for people who hunt or look for something, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Los Angeles artist admitting very immature form

parts.note: the usual abbreviation for the Californian city

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the artist lets another letter inside

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, the crossword's standard artist
v is an abbreviation of very

explanation.surface: A painter in Hollywood lets in work that is still very juvenile.
explanation.walkthrough: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of Britain's Royal Academy of Arts.
explanation.definitionFit: Insects hatch as grubs or caterpillars, their early undeveloped stage before becoming adults.

clue.text: Unhappily abstain, lust being considerable

indicators.note: things going unhappily go wrong, so the letters fall into disorder

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone grudgingly gives up a great deal of desire.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something large in amount or size, so they are close synonyms.

clue.text: Unpleasant, chased by police

parts.note: ran after, pursued
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: A disagreeable suspect is pursued by officers.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is the plain-clothes detective branch of a British police force.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancid literally describes stale, foul-smelling fat, and more loosely anything nasty or offensive.

clue.text: Steward at start of trip unusually tanned

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: arranged in an unusual way, the letters do not keep their normal order
the start of a word is its opening letter alone

parts.note: opening letter of trip
taken as written

explanation.surface: A flight steward begins a journey with a surprising suntan.
explanation.definitionFit: A steward is someone who waits upon passengers or guests, as an attendant does.

clue.text: Surprise in contract

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to come upon someone unexpectedly
second meaning: to pick up an illness

explanation.surface: An unexpected twist hidden in a legal agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: Contract suggests a legal document, but here it is the verb used of illness.
explanation.definitionFit: You can catch a thief in the act, surprising them, and catch a cold, contracting it.

clue.text: Resolve, endlessly receiving pressure, at this point cracked

indicators.note: without its end the word loses its final letter
a word receiving others takes them inside itself

parts.note: decide, to resolve, with its last letter dropped
p is the symbol for pressure in physics
here means at this place or point

explanation.surface: Under strain, someone's resolve finally breaks at this moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cracked' looks like part of the story of breaking under pressure, but it is the definition, as in cracking a code.
explanation.definitionFit: Cracking a code or cipher means working it out, which is exactly what deciphering it does.

clue.text: Verbal attack reflected support by social group

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror shows things the wrong way round

parts.note: aid is help or support
a tribe is a social group

explanation.surface: A tribe considers the backing it gets and launches a tirade.
explanation.definitionFit: A diatribe is a bitter spoken or written denunciation, a tirade of abuse against someone.

clue.text: Still endless criticism about volunteers

indicators.note: with no end the word drops its final letter
to be about something is to surround it

parts.note: stick, meaning harsh criticism, with its last letter dropped
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: Volunteers keep on receiving an unending stream of complaints.
explanation.walkthrough: To give someone stick is British slang for criticising them; the Territorial Army is Britain's part-time volunteer force.
explanation.definitionFit: Something static is motionless, not moving at all, which is what still means as an adjective.

clue.text: Excited fans stir champ to show skill

indicators.note: excited things are stirred up, so their letters get thrown about

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Thrilled supporters spur on their champion to display his ability.
explanation.definitionFit: Craftsmanship is the expertise or artistry of a skilled maker, so it names a kind of skill.

clue.text: Actress, knowing about upset, in bad temper

indicators.note: in a down answer, upsetting turns the pieces upside down so they read bottom to top
the reversed pieces go inside the jumbled word
a bad version of the word is a corrupted one with its letters jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
sly means knowing or artful
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A star actress, aware of the turmoil, flies into a rage.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upset' turns the joined pieces upside down; 'bad temper' looks like the actress's mood but is the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Meryl Streep is an American film star, winner of three Oscars, so she is an example of an actress.

clue.text: Approval for each assignment

parts.note: per means for each, as in per head
a mission is an assigned task

explanation.surface: Each assignment must be signed off before it goes ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Granting permission means giving consent or authorisation, the same idea as approval.

clue.text: Observe, with obvious hesitation, startling event

parts.note: to eye something is to watch it
open means plain or obvious, as in open secret
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: Someone watches, clearly unsure, as something shocking happens.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye-opener is a surprising revelation, something that makes you see things afresh.

clue.text: Exploitative pose assumed by soldier in charge

indicators.note: something assumed is taken on or taken in, so it sits within the other pieces

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper
to sit for a portrait is to pose
i/c is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: An officer in command strikes a pose that takes advantage of others.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasite lives off its host, so parasitic behaviour feeds on and exploits other people.

clue.text: Passage in article with silly lies

parts.note: the indefinite article

indicators.note: silly suggests nonsense, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A newspaper article is full of foolish untruths.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a walkway between rows of seats, a passage through a church, plane or shop.

clue.text: Astonished head of government's in step with revolutionary

indicators.note: the letter sits inside the word that follows

parts.note: a stage is a step in a process

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: opening letter of government
red is a common term for a communist revolutionary

explanation.surface: A prime minister is amazed to find himself marching alongside a radical.
explanation.definitionFit: Staggered as an adjective means so shocked or amazed as to be thrown off balance.

clue.text: Skinflint lives alone finally in room after retirement

indicators.note: the pieces are placed inside the other word
retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: rm is the abbreviation for room

indicators.note: finally points to the very last letter of the preceding word

parts.note: last letter of alone
is means exists or lives

explanation.surface: A tight-fisted pensioner lives on his own in a single room.
explanation.definitionFit: A miser hoards money and hates spending, exactly the character of a skinflint.

clue.text: Awkward guy at back of house, very withdrawn

indicators.note: when something is withdrawn it is taken away, so those letters leave the word
being at the back of something places this piece after the other

parts.note: villa, a house, with v for very removed
to guy someone is to mock or tease them

explanation.surface: A shy man lurks behind the house, very introverted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Withdrawn' seems to describe the shy guy, but it removes V (very) from VILLA. Guy as a verb is an old word for ridicule.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone ill at ease feels uncomfortable and self-conscious, socially awkward.

clue.text: Hysterical team becoming disunited

parts.note: a side is a sports team
splitting means breaking apart

explanation.surface: A squad is falling apart in a frenzy of emotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hysterical' suggests panic, but here it means extremely funny.
explanation.definitionFit: Hysterical informally means hilarious, and side-splitting describes laughter so hard it hurts.

clue.text: Digger's first turn releasing soft piece of turf

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of that word is used

parts.note: opening letter of digger

indicators.note: releasing something lets it go, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: to pivot is to turn
p is piano, soft in music

explanation.surface: A gardener's first spin with the spade lifts up a clod of grass.
explanation.definitionFit: A divot is a chunk of grass and earth gouged out, typically by a golf club.

clue.text: Department getting some praise recently

indicators.note: only some of the following words are taken, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A government department has recently won some approval.
explanation.walkthrough: A département is an administrative region of France, named here after the Isère river.
explanation.definitionFit: Isère is one of France's départements, in the Alps around Grenoble.

clue.text: Happy with piece of publicity following good line

indicators.note: following means coming after, so this piece is placed last

parts.note: g is an abbreviation for good
l is an abbreviation for line
an ad is an advertisement

explanation.surface: Someone is pleased with a nice bit of press coverage.
explanation.definitionFit: Glad and happy are everyday synonyms for feeling pleased or cheerful.

clue.text: Encourage appeal in stirring vein

indicators.note: the short piece goes inside the mixed-up word
a stirred mixture is churned up, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written
it means sex appeal, charm

explanation.surface: A rousing tone is used to coax and plead.
explanation.walkthrough: IT for appeal comes from the 1920s 'It girl', one with sex appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: To invite trouble or comment is to encourage or provoke it, a sense of tempting or asking for.

clue.text: Be clear, worried about king being intellectual

indicators.note: to go about something is to surround it
worried letters are fretted over and pulled out of their order

parts.note: taken as written
R is for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: An anxious monarch is told to speak plainly and think hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Cerebral relates to the brain, so it describes someone or something bookish, governed by thought.

clue.text: Number with link receiving constant attention

parts.note: no. is the abbreviation for number

indicators.note: a word receiving a letter takes it inside itself

parts.note: a tie is a link or bond
c is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light

explanation.surface: A figure with a steady connection gets steady regard.
explanation.definitionFit: To take notice of something is to pay it heed, so the noun means attention.

clue.text: Excellent price attached to object protected by cover

parts.note: SP is starting price in horse-race betting

indicators.note: something protected is shielded within its guard, so it sits inside

parts.note: a lid covers a container
an end is an aim or object

explanation.surface: A price tag is stuck on an item kept under wraps.
explanation.walkthrough: SP, the starting price, is the betting odds on a horse at the start of a race.
explanation.definitionFit: Splendid is a British-sounding word of praise meaning superb or magnificent, a synonym for first-rate.
